newsitem.title: CHINA: Hong Kong stocks stage rebound, close higher.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong stocks stage rebound, close higher.

text.p: Hong Kong stocks staged a rebound on Wednesday, erasing morning losses to end the session firm as selling dried up in the property sector and bargain hunters pushed prices higher.

The Hang Seng Index closed on a gain of 99.52 points, or 0.61 percent, at 16,482.93 after tumbling to a low of 16,176.32 in morning trade. Turnover rose to HK$28.17 billion compared with HK$27.93 billion on Tuesday.
"It's a technical rebound," said Henry Lui, research analyst at Mansion House Research. "Many property stocks rebounded significantly from their lows," he said.
Shares in Cheung Kong (Holdings) Ltd ended on a gain of HK$0.75 at HK$93.00 after slumping to HK$91.00 earlier in the session.
Sun Hung Kai Properties Ltd ended down HK$0.75 at HK$99.25 but off a low of HK$96.75 and Henderson Land Development Co Ltd rose HK$2.50 to HK$73.00.
The Hang Seng Index's early decline was prompted by an overnight fall on Wall Street and added to a drop of 264 points over Monday and Tuesday's sessions.

"If Wall street rebounds tonight, you might see another sort of a rebounding day for local stocks tomorrow," said Lui. H-shares continued to surge on Wednesday, with the index of Hong Kong-listed China enterprises rising 94.75 points, or 6.61 percent, to 1,528.70.
"This is still due to excess liquidity in the market and speculation of further restructuring within the H-share group," said Peter So, deputy head of research at Schroder Securities.
Shares in First Tractor Co Ltd surged HK$0.80 to HK$6.50 and Zhenhai Refining & Chemical Co Ltd advanced HK$0.875 to HK$4.80.

"It is really hard to quantify what kind of impact this kind of restructuring or merger, if any, will have but investors are looking at H-shares as a short-term speculative punt," said Lui. Red chips were also strong, with the Hang Seng China Affiliated Corporatations Index closing 109.95 points, or 2.93 percent, higher at 3,860.62.
China Resources Enterprise Ltd, also a component of the blue chip index, rose HK$1.80 to HK$38.80.
Kah Wah Bank Ltd surged HK$1.45 to HK$10.90 and Union Bank of Hong Kong Ltd advanced HK$1.65 to HK$20.75.

Trading in Shangri-La Asia Ltd shares was suspended on Wednesday. The company posted a 6.3 percent fall in interim net profit to HK$470.95 million and said it planned to buy 100 percent of hotel management company SLIM International Ltd.
